title: The Trophy at Table Nine
intro: A board-game café's Friday tournament. At 21:40 the lights went out for ninety seconds. When they came back, the champion's trophy was gone from the shelf behind the counter. Four people were close enough to reach it.

D.name: Ruben Ash
D.detail: Arrived at 21:35 with pizzas and is still here.

evidence.text: The main switch was flipped by hand, not blown. A smear of red ink from a pizza box is on the lever.
A dust outline where the trophy stood, and a cardboard pizza-box insert left in its place, cut to the trophy's height so it looked like the trophy in the dark.
Empty except for the receipt: four pizzas, delivered 21:35, signed ‘I. Sato’.

A.text: I was at the till the whole blackout. The drawer beeps if it opens, and nobody heard it.
A.truth: Mara's account checks out; the till log confirms nobody opened the drawer.

B.text: I'd already gone outside to cool off. I came back in when the lights came on.
B.truth: Theo was outside during the blackout, cooling off after the semi-final.

C.text: I never touched the pizzas. I was at Table Nine with the finalists.
C.truth: Fine. I signed for the pizzas at the counter at 21:35, right next to the shelf.

D.text: I never went past the counter. I left the boxes on the first table and waited by the door.
D.truth: Okay, I flipped the switch. Ivy gave me ten bucks and the key and said it was a prank for the finalists.

solution.text: Ivy Sato held the fuse-box key and gave it to Ruben to flip the switch. She signed for the pizzas to get beside the shelf, then left the cut cardboard as a stand-in. The trophy was already listed for sale online under a fake name.

endings.C: Case closed. Chat, you'd make a fine detective.
endings.D: Ruben flipped the switch, but he never touched the trophy. The judge walks out with it.
endings.default: That suspect's account is cleared. The evidence points to Ivy Sato: she arranged the blackout, took the trophy, and left a cardboard stand-in. It was already listed for sale online under a fake name.
